concepts.definition: A plain text table in which each row is a record and the columns are separated by commas; the first row is the column names.
concepts.example: Under the header zaman,sicaklik_C,nem_yuzde, each measurement is added as one row.
concepts.pitfall: Writing a different number of columns in the header row and the data rows.

concepts.definition: A layout that writes the moment of the measurement as year-month-day hour:minute:second, with the month and day in two digits.
concepts.example: 2026-03-14 08:30:05 reads the same in every country and lines up in time order even when sorted as text.
concepts.pitfall: Leaving the month and day as single digits (2026-3-9); the sorting goes wrong.

concepts.definition: A function that builds a CSV row from a time and two numbers, without touching the hardware.
concepts.example: The output of satirOlustur(DateTime(2026,1,5,7,8,9), 21.0, NAN) can be tried with fixed values.
concepts.pitfall: Writing separate formatting code for each place (Serial, SD); the row format comes out different in the two places.

concepts.definition: When the sensor cannot be read, the float becomes NaN; in CSV this is shown by leaving the field empty.
concepts.example: The third row is written as 2026-07-09 23:59:59,, so the timestamp stays and the columns do not shift.
concepts.pitfall: Trying to turn NaN into text, or skipping that row and not keeping the record at all.

concepts.definition: An AVR function that turns a float into text with a given width and number of decimal places.
concepts.example: dtostrf(23.5, 1, 1, tampon) writes "23.5" into the buffer.
concepts.pitfall: Thinking sprintf works with %f; on AVR it is not supported by default.

concepts.definition: The decimal mark inside a number and the character that separates the columns must not get mixed up.
concepts.example: For Excel set to Turkish, the format 23,5;55,0 (decimal comma, semicolon separator) can be used.
concepts.pitfall: If a decimal comma and a comma separator are used together, 23,5 is split into two columns.

quiz.prompt:
What appears on the Serial monitor when the call below runs? (satirOlustur is the function from the lesson: two-digit fields, numbers with one decimal place, an empty field for NaN.)

```
Serial.println(satirOlustur(DateTime(2026, 1, 5, 7, 8, 9), 21.0, NAN));
```
quiz.explanation: ikiHane() pads the month, day, hour, minute and second to two digits. Because dtostrf gives 1 decimal place, 21.0 is written. Because the humidity is NaN, the last field stays empty; no zero is written, and the comma at the end of the row keeps the number of columns.

options: The year should be two digits instead of year()
A slash should be used instead of the dash
s = should be used instead of s +=
month() and day() are not written with two digits; ikiHane() should be used
quiz.explanation: month() and day() do not add a leading zero. When "2026-3-9" and "2026-12-01" are compared as text, "2026-1" is compared with "2026-3"; month 12 is sorted before month 3. Written with two digits it becomes "2026-03-09", and text order matches time order.

quiz.prompt: A logger writes the row with a comma separator and a decimal comma, like this: 2026-03-14 08:30:05,23,5,55,0. How many columns does a spreadsheet program read this row as?
quiz.explanation: The row is split at the commas: "2026-03-14 08:30:05", "23", "5", "55", "0". Instead of the expected 3 columns, there are 5. The fix is to use a point for the decimal or to make the separator a semicolon.

quiz.prompt: Why is writing the millis() value (for example 123456) as the timestamp not good enough?
options: millis() resets every time the board switches on; it does not tell you the row's real date and time
millis() cannot be written to CSV because it is a number
millis() must always be divided by 1000
CSV files can only contain text
quiz.explanation: millis() gives the time since the board switched on and starts from zero when the board restarts. Someone who opens the file a year later cannot find out when the row was written. The date and time taken from the RTC give the real time. There is no problem writing numbers to CSV.

quiz.prompt: The device writes a row every 5 seconds. If it runs for one day (24 hours) without stopping, how many data rows are added to the file? (Do not count the header row.)
quiz.explanation: There are 24 × 60 × 60 = 86400 seconds in a day. 86400 ÷ 5 = 17280 rows. This calculation is used to estimate how fast the card fills up when choosing the measurement interval.
